title: Three Triangles from One Point
statement: Square $ABCD$ has side length $12$. A point $P$ lies inside the square, and triangles $PAB$ and $PBC$ have areas $20$ and $30$. Find the area of triangle $PAC$.
hints: Work out how far $P$ is from the line $AB$ and from the line $BC$.
Put $B$ at the origin with $BC$ along the $x$-axis and $BA$ along the $y$-axis. Then you know $P$ exactly, and you can see which side of $AC$ it lies on.
solution: Put $B = (0, 0)$, $C = (12, 0)$ and $A = (0, 12)$, and let $P = (x, y)$. Then $[PAB] = 6x = 20$ and $[PBC] = 6y = 30$, so $P = (\frac{10}{3}, 5)$. The line $AC$ is $x + y = 12$, and $x + y = \frac{25}{3}$, so $P$ is at distance $\frac{11}{3\sqrt{2}}$ from it. Since $AC = 12\sqrt{2}$, $[PAC] = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 12\sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{11}{3\sqrt{2}} = 22$.

solution_figures.alt: Square with B at the origin, C = (12, 0) on the x-axis and A = (0, 12) on the y-axis, and the fourth vertex D. Point P = (10/3, 5) lies below the diagonal AC. Triangles PAB and PBC are shaded with areas 20 and 30, and triangle PAC is highlighted with area 22.
